text: i18n: UI strings are English-only; no localization layer

Part 1/3 landed in 42bc831: the web i18n layer (locales.ts, messages/en.ts, index.tsx with I18nProvider/useT), wired at the app root, plus a first tranche of migrated strings. Ships English only. Two decisions worth knowing for the rest of the work: (1) the context default is functional rather than null, so useT works outside a provider and components stay unit-testable as isolated subtrees, while setLocale throws because that IS a real bug — this avoided wrapping all nine existing page tests and every future one; (2) pure functions like formatLastSeen take t as a parameter rather than reaching for a hook, which is what keeps their tests able to assert exact wording. Also: localStorage persistence of the chosen locale ended up in the provider rather than in T-127, since that is where the locale state lives and splitting it would have meant touching the provider twice — T-127 is now purely the two UI surfaces. Remaining: ~150 more web strings (concentrated in ListPropsPage, ItemDialog, SettingsPage, LoginPage), then the Android layer and its ~205 strings.

Parts 2-3 landed (7862a0d, 5dd5bd3): LoginPage, RedeemPage, SyncIndicator, ItemDialog, ListPropsPage migrated; syncStatus and relativeTime now share one set of ago.* keys rather than carrying identical copies of the same four labels. Android decision made rather than deferred: CompositionLocalProvider with a localized Context, NOT AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales. Reasons — it yields LocalLayoutDirection, which is exactly the hook T-126 needs for Arabic, and it avoids dragging the AppCompat theming stack into a pure Compose/Material3 app. Its one real gap is strings resolved outside composition (the collaborator-change notification poster), to be closed explicitly with a localized-context helper rather than ignored. Accepted cost: no integration with Android's system per-app-language screen, which matters little for an APK-distributed self-hosted app. Remaining: SettingsPage/AdminPage/OverviewPage/ListPage leftovers (~30 web strings), then the Android layer and its ~205 strings.
